lines.text: A giant AI just walked out of the data center.
On October 15, Meta released Muse Spark Open, built with help from Apple.
Myth number one: an AI this powerful only runs in a huge data center.
Fact: Meta tuned it to run on just two Mac Studios with Apple's M5 Ultra chip.
And anyone can download its weights from Hugging Face.
Myth number two: open AI models are just small toys.
Fact: it has 816 billion parameters, but only about 42 billion switch on for each token.
And it can read up to a million tokens at once.
One catch: its license limits some commercial use. Would you run AI at home?
